newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae says eyes global bond in lire.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae says eyes global bond in lire.

text.p: U.S. home loans group Fannie Mae said it was considering a global bond in lire in its continuous quest to broaden its investor base, its treasurer Linda Knight told a news conference on Thursday.
"There is tremendous interest in Italy for a potential retail deal to tap the savings," Knight said.
"(The global bond) would be denominated in lire and then swapped back into dollars."
With regards to the long-awaited French franc global bond, she said swap market conditions were still not ideal for such an issue.
"We haven't been able to make a French franc global work."
Fannie Mae launched the first sterling global bond in mid-February which was snapped up by international investors in Britain, Asia, Continental Europe and the U.S.
"We'd love to come back and do deals in markets where we have already been successful, like marks and sterling," Knight said.

When asked about clauses on Eurobonds denominated in European currencies that may join the single currency after the third stage of European economic and monetary union, she said Fannie Mae felt covered for this event.
"We have in our global debt facility some language that allows us to redeem securities in successor currencies so we think that already covers us."
She said Fannie Mae's mark bonds that mature in 2001 and 2002 have been looked at and it was felt the "successor language" covered them.
Fannie Mae is rated triple-A by both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp.
